title: a post Instagram rejected ends as `failed` -- the slot and its photo are lost, and nothing re-books them
evidence: 1 post(s) marked failed in the last 24h (newest 9.7h ago): post 333 photo 339 slot 2026-09-20 15:15:13.541039 failed 2026-09-20 16:00:58.718029 reason: instagram: 400 code 9007 (Media ID is not available -- the media is not ready for publishing); backfilled 2026-09-20 from log/scheduled_posting.log (row predates failure_reason). packs/scheduling/lib/tasks/scheduled_posting.rake calls record_failure! with no requeue (the row's failure_reason carries the cause; rows written before 2026-09-20 have none, so grep the post id in log/scheduled_posting.log for those). Nothing else can see it: check_publish_liveness counts only scheduled/draft rows past due, and check_publish_gap measures the newest POSTED post. The original failure mode is fixed in-repo -- Instagram::Client retries a 9007 'media not ready' publish 4x/10s and the row persists its reason -- so what lands here has already survived the retry; it ages out of this window on its own.

notes.note: 2026-09-20 19:4xZ ops-triage: the TRANSIENT half of the no-retry defect is now FIXED in-repo (commit ffe9692). Root cause of the 9007 class: Instagram answers the container status check status_code=FINISHED, then rejects the immediate publish with 400 code 9007/subcode 2207027 'media is not ready for publishing'; the client published with no tolerance and the publisher has no requeue, so the slot AND its photo were lost. Instagram::Client now classifies that response (MediaNotReadyError) and retries the publish 4x, 10s apart; every other error and the last attempt fail exactly as before. Verified: spec/services/scheduling/instagram_client_spec.rb is RED on the unfixed client (2 failures) and green after; full suite 409 examples / 0 failures; adjacent specs green. REMAINING (needs Tim): a post that definitively fails still consumes its slot with no requeue -- is a missed slot made up, or dropped? That is a product policy call, not a code defect.
